subject: Wintermute Dedicated Capacity: urgent slotting & cross-deal mitigation
messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Jensen <kim.j@wintermute.ai>, Procurement <procurement@wintermute.ai>

Subject: Wintermute Dedicated Capacity: urgent slotting & cross-deal mitigation

Hi Marissa / Rishi —

Quick note: our RL inference rollout that we discussed in Q1 is hitting an aggressive launch window (traffic ramp expected 2028-04-10 through 2028-04-24). Per our committed capacity (see SOW WIN-2028-committed-64) we need the 64-GPU pool to be available for sustained throughput during that two-week window.

We just received notice that another existing Dedicated customer (internal scheduling name: “Nimbus Labs”) has a short-term surge scheduled for the same region during part of that window. There's potential overlap of ~48 GPU-hours per day for five days.

Can you confirm whether slotting or temporary reassignments are possible? If we need to accept reduced throughput, Procurement wants to understand compensatory credits or sprint-level burst guarantees.

Attaching our request doc with exact window and expected p99 latency targets.

[Attachment: capacity_request_wintermute.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Wintermute Dedicated Capacity: urgent slotting & cross-deal mitigation

Thanks for the heads-up, Alex — and for the attachment. I dug into the schedule and the overlap looks like a five-day hot window where both deals need sustained capacity in the same shard.

Immediate thoughts / options we can mobilize quickly:
- Temporal slotting: stagger peak windows by 4–8 hours per day for one of the parties to reduce simultaneous load.
- Burst credits / compensated reduction: offer Wintermute a negotiated burst allotment + one-time account credit if they accept a 15% throughput degradation during the highest-overlap days.
- Hot-lane pre-warm: ops can pin a small warm pool (12 GPUs) for Wintermute to keep p99 acceptable while the rest is shared.
- Short-term model variant: if a quantized variant is acceptable we can reduce GPU time per token (Ops + Rishi to confirm feasibility).

I'm attaching a capacity matrix (v2) with proposed slotting permutations. Can we set a 30-min alignment call tomorrow to pick one? If Procurement requires credits formalized, we'll loop Legal/Finance — that can be quick if we stick to a simple credit + burst structure.

[Attachment: capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx)]

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Torrance <alex.t@wintermute.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Apr 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Wintermute Dedicated Capacity: urgent slotting & cross-deal mitigation

Marissa / Alex — quick technical context from infra: we evaluated the Wintermute model and there are three constraints that matter for mitigation decisions:
1) Quantization: their model loses >6% QA in our internal eval when moving from fp16 to the quantized variant for their RL policy. Not acceptable without additional A/B validation.
2) Cold-start cost: if we preempt and then re-allocate, the KV warm-up cost is ~8–12 minutes per instance which will spike p95/p99 during the swap.
3) Warm pool sizing: to maintain p99 < target, we need a warm pool of ~12–16 GPUs for the peak minutes. Smaller pools will push latency above Wintermute's target.

Operationally I recommend:
- Reserve a 12-GPU hot-lane for Wintermute during the peak window (this minimizes p99 impact and keeps token cost manageable).
- Implement an automated slotting window: overlap days 2028-04-12 through 2028-04-16, allow dynamic shuffling outside of peak hours.
- If Wintermute agrees to a small credit (per earlier suggestion from Marissa), we can use that to pay for pre-warm time and keep SLAs tight.

If Sales can confirm credits/terms by end of day Monday, we can have Ops implement pinning and schedule the maintenance adjustments in time.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Alex Torrance <alex.t@wintermute.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@wintermute.ai>, Kimberly Jensen <kim.j@wintermute.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Apr 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Wintermute Dedicated Capacity: urgent slotting & cross-deal mitigation

Marissa / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed your matrix and Rishi's notes with the engineering team. We cannot accept the QA hit from quantization and cold-starts are a real concern for our production SLAs.

We are prepared to accept a temporary arrangement if Redwood can: (a) guarantee the 12-GPU hot-lane pinned for our peak minutes, (b) provide an additional 48 GPU-hours of burst capacity to cover traffic spikes, and (c) issue a service credit equivalent to one week of Dedicated fees (applied if p99 exceeds target during the overlap).

Procurement would like the commitment in writing (simple addendum / DocuSign) by Monday EOD so we can finalize internal rollout plans. Happy to sign an addendum if Legal/Finance can provide the DocuSign link.

Thanks — Alex

Subject: Re: Wintermute Dedicated Capacity: urgent slotting & cross-deal mitigation

Alex — appreciated the clear ask and procurement timeline. We're aligned on the approach. Summary of the decision and next steps:

Decision (agreed):
- Redwood will pin a 12-GPU hot-lane for Wintermute for the peak minutes during 2028-04-12 to 2028-04-16.
- We will allocate an additional 48 GPU-hours as burst capacity available to Wintermute during that window.
- If p99 exceeds the agreed threshold during the overlap days, Redwood will apply a service credit equal to one week of Dedicated fees for Wintermute (to be formalized in addendum).

Action items:
1) Sales (Marissa) to coordinate with Legal/Finance to produce a one-page addendum and DocuSign link by EOD Monday (HUBSPOT-123456).
2) Ops (Rishi) to implement the pin + warm-pool config and run a short smoke test on 2028-04-10.
3) Engineering (Ben) to prepare a brief runbook for hot-lane failover and monitoring hooks to surface p99 in real time.
4) Wintermute Procurement to sign the addendum and confirm the billing contact.

I've attached the slotting decision summary for internal records. Please reply-all to confirm acceptance and I'll route the addendum to DocuSign.

[Attachment: slotting_decision_summary.pdf (pdf)]
